claims.content: When the three QMPNN variants QGCN, QGAT, and QSAGE of standard GNN architectures are trained under the same hyperparameters as those standard GNN architectures and evaluated on standard datasets, the quaternion models achieve comparable or better accuracy, ROC-AUC, or Hits@K (proportion of top-K predictions that are correct) while using roughly one-fourth of the trainable parameters of those standard GNN architectures.
On CORA link prediction, QGCN attains ROC-AUC 83.55 ± 0.03 with 27.2K parameters, compared to GCN's ROC-AUC 79.27 ± 0.47 with 96.0K parameters.

## 5 Experiments
The effectiveness of QMPNNs for different GNN variants is validated with extensive experimentation on different real-world standard datasets. We also verify the existence of the GLTs as per our definition. We evaluated their performance on three tasks, node classification, link prediction, and graph classification.

Table 4: Link prediction on various datasets including CORA, CITESEER, PUBMED, and OBGL-COLLAB. ROC-AUC and Hits@50 values are reported with their standard deviations, along with the corresponding GFLOPs (denoted as GF) and parameter counts (in K units, denoted as GF).
